{{Nihongo|'''Rui Hachimura'''|八村 塁|Hachimura Rui|born February 8, 1998}} is a Japanese [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] and is a current member of the [[Japan national basketball team|Japanese national team]]. Listed at {{height|ft=6|in=8}} and 230 lbs (104 kg), he plays both the [[small forward]] and [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions.<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Rui Hachimura |url=https://gozags.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2524 |publisher=Gonzaga University Athletics |accessdate=November 22, 2018}}</ref> He is considered one of the top prospects for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref name="education">{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=The education of Gonzaga's Rui Hachimura |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25288415/the-education-gonzaga-rui-hachimura |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=November 22, 2018 |date=November 16, 2018}}</ref><ref name="spokesman">{{cite web |title=Rui Hachimura |url=http://www.spokesman.com/zags/rosters/player/rui-hachimura/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=November 22, 2018}}</ref>

Born in [[Toyama Prefecture]], Hachimura achieved success at the youth level in Japan, leading Meisei High School to three straight All-Japan High School Tournament titles and being a top player for the Japanese [[Japan national under-17 basketball team|under-17]] and [[Japan national under-19 basketball team|under-19]] national teams in [[FIBA]] competition. He joined Gonzaga in 2016 as the fifth Japanese-born men's [[NCAA Division I]] player and became the first Japanese national in 2017 to play in the [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Division I men's tournament]]. As a sophomore, he earned first-team All-WCC honors. He was named a finalist for the Naismith Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woodburn |first1=Peter |title=Rui Hachimura named Naismith Player of the Year finalist |url=https://www.slipperstillfits.com/2019/3/19/18272778/naismith-player-of-the-year-finalist-rui-hachimura |website=The Slipper Still Fits |publisher=SB Nation |accessdate= March 22, 2019}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
[[File:Hachimura rui (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|Hachimura with Meisei High School in 2016]]
Hachimura was born in [[Toyama Prefecture]] of Japan to a Japanese mother, Makiko, and [[Benin]]ese father, Zakari. His name "Rui"(塁） literally means "baseball base" in Japanese, It was reportedly given to him by his grandfather because he was a big fan of baseball. He has three younger siblings, one brother, and two sisters. Hachimura's younger brother, Allen, is a basketball player at Tokai University in Japan

Hopefully he's hitting books hard instead of coming to #AST2016|url=https://twitter.com/heinnews/status/714424351085473793|date=March 28, 2016}}</ref> In May 2016, Hachimura announced that he met the SAT and GPA requirements to be eligible to play at Gonzaga beginning as early as fall 2016. He planned to play as a true freshman and did not redshirt his first year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hachimura cleared to enroll at Gonzaga|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2016/05/11/basketball/hachimura-cleared-to-enroll-at-gonzaga/#.VzNEH4QrLIW|date=May 11, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
Hachimura made his regular season debut for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]] on November 11, 2016 against [[Utah Valley Wolverines men's basketball|Utah Valley]], recording 1 point and 3 rebounds in 4 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nov 11, 2016 - Utah Valley 69, Gonzaga 92 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/boxscore/2016-11-11/Utah-Valley-at-Gonzaga/248588 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=November 22, 2018 |date=November 11, 2016}}</ref> As a result, he became the fifth Japanese-born player to ever play [[NCAA Division I]] basketball.<ref name="media">{{cite web |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Gonzaga forward Rui Hachimura at the center of Japanese media’s attention |url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2017/nov/11/gonzaga-forward-rui-hachimura-at-the-center-of-jap/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |accessdate=November 22, 2018 |date=November 11, 2017}}</ref> On December 1, he scored a season-high 10 points in 13 minutes in a 97–63 win over [[Mississippi Valley State Delta Devils men's basketball|Mississippi Valley State]].<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 8 Gonzaga breezes past Mississippi Valley State 97-63 |url=https://gozags.com/news/2016/12/1/No_8_Gonzaga_breezes_past_Mississippi_Valley_State_97_63.aspx |publisher=Gonzaga University Athletics |accessdate=November 22, 2018 |date=December 1, 2016}}</ref> Hachimura scored 8 points on February 23, 2017 against [[San Diego Toreros men's basketball|San Diego]], helping his team win the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) title.<ref>{{cite web |title=Feb 23, 2017 - Gonzaga 96, San Diego 38 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/boxscore/2017-02-23/Gonzaga-at-San-Diego/248609 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=November 22, 2018 |date=February 23, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Top-ranked MBB Remains Perfect, Beats San Diego 96-38 |url=https://gozags.com/news/2017/2/23/Top_ranked_MBB_Remains_Perfect_Beats_San_Diego_96_38.aspx |publisher=Gonzaga University Athletics |accessdate=November 22, 2018 |date=February 24, 2017}}</ref> On March 16, 2017, after playing 1 minute against [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]], he became the first Japanese native to ever appear in the [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Division I men's tournament]].<ref name=Mandel>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/gonzaga-rui-hachimura-ncaa-tournament-final-four-japan-033017 |title=Japan will be watching the Final Four just to see this guy you probably don’t know |first=Stewart |last=Mandel |publisher=Fox Sports |date=March 30, 2017 |accessdate=July 17, 2017}}</ref> Through 28 games as a freshman, Hachimura averaged 2.6 points and 1.4 rebounds while shooting 53 percent from the field in 4.6 minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2016-2017/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND|title=Season Box Score|website=gozags.com|access-date=2017-04-18}}</ref>

In the 2017–18 campaign, Hachimura appeared in 37 games for Gonzaga, including two starts, averaging 11.6 points and 4.7 rebounds per contest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2017-2018/teamcume.html#TEAM.IND|title=2017-18 Gonzaga Men's Basketball Season Box Score|website=gozags.com|access-date=2018-03-27}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:20180917 FIBA Basketball World Cup Qualifier Japan vs Iran (44019576184).jpg|right|200px|thumb|Hachimura after a 2019 FIBA World Cup qualification game with Japan]]
Hachimura represents [[Japan national basketball team|Japan]] internationally. At the 2013 FIBA Asia U16 Championship in Iran, he averaged 22.8 points, 12.6 rebounds and 2.8 blocks through eight contests,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Rui Hachimura profile, FIBA Asia U16 Championship for Men 2013 {{!}} FIBA.COM|url = https://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/110364/sid/6577/tid/309/_/2013_FIBA_Asia_U16_Championship_for_Men/index.html|website = FIBA.COM|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref> guiding his team to a third-place finish.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Schedule & results {{!}} 2013 FIBA Asia U16 Championship for Men {{!}} ARCHIVE.FIBA.COM|url = https://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/event/p/pid/110364/sid/6577/tid/309/_/2013_FIBA_Asia_U16_Championship_for_Men/schedule.html|website = www.fiba.com|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref> In April 2014, he played the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament|Albert-Schweitzer-Tournament]] in Germany with Japan's under 18 national team,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Cheeseball alert at 2014 Albert Schweitzer Tournament|url = http://www.fiba.com/news/Cheeseball-alert-at-2014-Albert-Schweitzer-Tournament|website = FIBA.com|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = AST 2014 Japan «  Deutscher Basketball Bund|url = http://www.basketball-bund.de/ligen-ergebnisse/albert-schweitzer-turnier/ast-2014-teams/ast-2014-japan|website = www.basketball-bund.de|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref> finishing in last place.<ref>{{Cite web|title = game stats / standings «  Deutscher Basketball Bund|url = http://www.basketball-bund.de/ligen-ergebnisse/albert-schweitzer-turnier/game-stats|website = www.basketball-bund.de|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref>

Japan finished the 2014 FIBA U17 World Championships 14th of 16 teams, with Hachimura scoring a tournament-high 22.6 points per game, while pulling down 6.6 boards and blocking 1.7 shots a contest.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Rui HACHIMURA at the Players of the 2014 FIBA U17 World Championship for Men - FIBA.com|url = http://www.fiba.com/world/u17/2014/Rui-HACHIMURA|website = FIBA.com|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref> During the tournament, he dropped 25 points on the USA team that went on to win the title; that team included four players who were chosen in the [[2017 NBA draft]] in [[Jayson Tatum]], [[Josh Jackson (basketball)|Josh Jackson]], [[Caleb Swanigan]], and [[Ivan Rabb]], plus other future college stars such as [[Diamond Stone]] and [[Malik Newman]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = United States of America v Japan - 12 Aug - FIBA.com|url = http://www.fiba.com/world/u17/2014/1208/USA-Japan#%7Ctab=boxscore_statistics|website = FIBA.com|access-date = 2016-02-20}}</ref><ref name=Mandel/>

He competed for Japan in the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], averaging team-bests 20.6 points and 11.0 rebounds a contest.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/fr/world/u19/2017/Japan|title=Japon at the FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2017 - FIBA.basketball|website=FIBA.basketball|language=fr|access-date=2017-07-09}}</ref> In a qualification round for the [[2019 FIBA World Cup]], Hachimura scored 25 points to help Japan defeat Iran 70-56.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=Rui Hachimura scores 25 as Japan upsets Iran in World Cup qualifier |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/09/18/rui-hachimura-scores-25-as-japan-upsets-iran-in-world-cup-qualifier/ |accessdate=September 21, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=September 18, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On April 15, 2019, Hachimura announced that he would forgo his final year of eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Gonzaga's Rui Hachimura Declares for NBA Draft|author=Jones, Kaelen|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/04/15/rui-hachimura-gonzaga-declares-nba-draft|date=April 15, 2019|accessdate=May 9, 2019|work=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>
